title: 34 Years Ago, Shonen Jump’s Coolest Anime Began By Killing Its Hero
content:
Yu Yu Hakusho began airing on October 10th, 1992, in Japan, and since then, its legacy as one of the greatest Shonen Jump series remains unmatched. Shueisha’s Shonen Jump magazines have dominated the anime and manga industry for several decades now. Most of the popular Shonen series you have come across over the decades are tied to the publisher’s magazines. This is especially the case for Weekly Shonen Jump , the manga magazine which was launched in 1969 in Japan. It eventually became the best-selling manga magazine thanks to the popularity of several classics such as One Piece, Dragon Ball, Naruto, and many more.

One of the magazine’s biggest manga during the 1990s was Yu Yu Hakusho , written and illustrated by Yoshihiro Togashi, the creator of Hunter x Hunter . While Hunter x Hunter remains his most successful work to date, it was Yu Yu Hakusho that helped him gain fame across Japan and later on in the West. The anime began airing decades ago, and even now, not many series can keep viewers hooked as it did. A huge reason behind its success is how it killed off its protagonist at the beginning of the story, after which the story took one unexpected turn after another.

Yu Yu Hakusho Begins With the Death of Yusuke Urameshi

On the surface, Yu Yu Hakusho doesn’t seem much different from a majority of Shonen series that follow the protagonist’s journey after they gain newfound powers in the very first episode. However, there’s one thing that completely sets it apart from any other show. Instead of going through the conventional route of having the protagonist gain power after some unexpected encounter, the story begins with the death of Yusuke Urameshi. As a 14-year-old delinquent, he used to spend his days skipping school and causing trouble for those around him. He would even get into fights with his rival Kazuma Kuwabara. If that wasn’t bad enough, Yusuke would also ridicule his childhood friend Keiko Yukimura with every opportunity he got.

His behavior stemmed from self-loathing and the burden he had to bear due to his alcoholic mother. However, when he saw a little boy in danger with the way of an oncoming car, he decided to sacrifice himself to save his life. Thanks to the intervention of the spirit guide Botan, after losing his life in the accident, Yusuke gains the opportunity to see how everyone around him reacted to his death. He never imagined that his death would cause so much grief to his mother and even his rival. However, due to his heroic deed, he gains an opportunity to return to life and become a Spirit Detective.

Yusuke begins solving a series of increasingly difficult paranormal mysteries while also befriending and battling demons along the way . His journey begins with his problematic life, but after getting a second chance, he turned everything around for himself and those close to him. What truly makes the series special is how it uses the death of the protagonist as the core narrative and the driving force right after the story kicks off. Not many people get a second chance in life, but when Yusuke did, he managed to fight for the good of the people and completely abandoned his delinquent lifestyle.

Yu Yu Hakusho Deserves a Reboot Now More Than Ever

The original anime was a massive success and, surprisingly enough, that’s exactly why the anime deserves a reboot. The 1990s animation style isn’t used anymore, which is why it’s increasingly difficult for series to attract new viewers. Not to mention that it was released in a long-running format, which was pretty common back in the day. Anime series were released two or three years after the manga, and both versions of the story would run new episodes or chapters every week.

Yu Yu Hakusho also followed the same format, but there’s a huge drawback when it comes to long-running anime adaptations. The uneven pacing and inconsistent animation couldn’t escape the viewers’ eyes. Not only that, but Togashi had to rush the Three Kings arc in the manga due to his health issues. It had the potential to be greater than what it already was. An anime reboot might also expand the arc into what Togashi initially envisioned.

Do you think Yusuke Urameshi’s shocking death made Yu Yu Hakusho one of the most memorable Shonen anime from the very beginning? Let us know in the comments!

title: Vinland Saga Fans Are Getting a Perfect Replacement in 2027
content:
It’s been over a year since the Vinland Saga manga reached its conclusion, and with the anime’s future uncertain, it’s obvious fans need a perfect replacement to keep them busy. Based on Makoto Yukimara’s manga, WIT Studio released the first season of the anime in 2019, but it was then handed over to MAPPA. The anime returned with a second season in 2023, but fans are still awaiting the third season, which is still awaiting an official confirmation. A recent update from the creator also confirms that Season 3 isn’t under production , so fans will have to wait longer than expected.

The manga has a total of four arcs, with the first two (the War Arc and the Slave Arc) being adapted into the first two seasons of the anime. This means that the anime still requires two more seasons to adapt the entire story. However, with no guarantee for the franchise’s future, there’s already a shortage of historical Seinen series, especially those that are well-written. Among the several incredible anime coming next year, Hitoshi Iwaaki’s 2003 manga, Historie , will premiere during the Winter anime lineup of 2027. While most global fans are most familiar with the creator because of Parasyte , not many knew about his underrated historical manga, Historie , until recently .

Historie Will Premiere in Winter 2027

While the anime hasn’t locked down an exact release date yet, it’s confirmed to be released in January 2027. Considering that the quarterly anime series debut around the first or second week of the month, we can expect the same for Historie as well. The anime also needs to confirm its streaming platform, but it will be announced shortly before the premiere. The manga began serialization in Kodansha’s Afternoon magazine in 2003, and it’s still ongoing. However, an anime adaptation by LINDENFILMS was announced in January this year, and it’s all set for its highly anticipated premiere.

One of the most exciting parts about this upcoming anime is that Nobunaga Shimazaki, the voice behind Shinichi Izumi in Parasyte: The Maxim , will play the role of Eumenes in Historie . There’s already a lot of hype around the series, especially since the manga won the 14th Japan Media Arts Festival Grand Prize in the Manga Division in 2010, and two years later, it was awarded the Grand Prize at the Osamu Tezuka Culture Prize. Since August 2024, the manga series has been published digitally in English by Kodansha and is available to read on the official K Manga app.

What Is the Plot of Historie ?

The story takes place in mid-14th century BC Greece, following a fictionalized account of Eumenes , who later became known throughout the world as the secretary and general of Alexander the Great. Even now, much about Eumenes’ history is a mystery, which is why Iwaaki took creative liberty to tell his version of his story. While Alexander is famous for being one of the greatest military commanders in history, Eumenes’ name is more or less forgotten by the world. The story follows a fictionalized version of his life before he gained fame as Alexander’s right-hand man.

In Iwaaki’s version of history, Eumenes was born into a wealthy family in the city-state of Cardia. As a boy, he was falsely accused of causing his adoptive father’s death and was sentenced to enslavement. The boy escaped the horrible life and embarked on a journey to find a new place in the world where he could belong. Thanks to his intellect and skills in warfare, he eventually became known far and wide for his genius, helping Alexander conquer major parts of the world. Before meeting the great ruler, Eumenes traveled great distances and overcame countless struggles while also befriending many influential figures of the time.

Although Alexander is one of the most famous historical figures of all time, Eumenes is an unsung genius whose story remains unknown to the world. While the narrative core of the series is significantly different than Vinland Saga , the themes of resilience and the coming-of-age story are something that fans are sure to love. While Thorfinn’s story centers around grief, regret, and redemption, Eumenes’s journey follows his exceptional story as a brilliant strategist.

Are you excited to see Historie bring its exceptional storytelling to anime, and do you think it can live up to the high standards set by Vinland Saga ? Let us know in the comments below!

title: 2 Years Ago, Dragon Ball Creator’s Final Project Marked the End of an Era
content:
As Akira Toriyama’s final project, Dragon Ball Daima received countless praises from fans who enjoyed a brand-new adventure of Goku and his friends. The 20-episode anime series was released last year to commemorate Dragon Ball ’s 40th anniversary. The story, written by Toriyama, serves as a sequel to DBZ, set a few years after the Buu Saga. Gomah, the new king of the Demon Realm, is horrified after witnessing the powers of Goku and the rest of the Z Warriors. Fearing that they would invade the Demon Realm, Gomah and his advisor, Degesu, conspired to use the Dragon Balls to turn the potential threats into children.

The anime premiered on October 11th, 2024, exactly two years ago. Following its exciting run, the series reached its conclusion in February next year, around the same time as Toriyama’s first death anniversary. The anime isn’t based on any manga , but the entire script and character designs were provided by the original creator, which made it all the more special to fans. This is the final project he ever worked on, and fans couldn’t help but feel bittersweet as they bid farewell to their favorite story. While Dragon Ball already has exciting anime projects planned for fans , it can’t be compared to an entirely new story by the beloved creator.

Dragon Ball Daima Breathed Life into the Most Underrated Super Saiyan Transformations

The anime first revived the Super Saiyan 3 transformation with Vegeta rather than Goku. The only time Goku used SSJ3 was in Dragon Ball Z when he had to stall Majin Buu in the Buu Saga. Unfortunately, Toriyama didn’t have the opportunity to further develop this transformation since the manga ended not long after that. Not to mention that Vegeta, who is usually one step behind Goku, didn’t achieve this transformation since the story ended shortly after that. By the time Dragon Ball Super was released, SSJ3 was more or less forgotten or just rarely discussed among fans.

A majority of fans were more focused on Super Saiyan God and Ultra Instinct, which introduced new and exciting forms that took over the internet. It became one of the least discussed transformations in the show, especially since it featured among some of the worst-animated moments, on top of other forms rendering it obsolete. Compared to that, Daima was able to adapt this old form with clean new animation to give it the proper amount of gravitas, unlike in Z, which mostly focused on a lot of the form’s drawbacks. However, it wasn’t even the most exciting part of the series since even SSJ4 got a new look for the first time in years.

While Super Saiyan 4 was originally revealed in the non-canon series Dragon Ball GT , Akira Toriyama reintroduced this form in his final project. Thanks to Neva using his magic to awaken Goku’s dormant powers, the Saiyan hero underwent a new transformation shortly before the anime finale. The transformation happened right before Gomah, the main villain of the anime, could deal a finishing blow, but luckily, Goku was easily able to overpower the villain.

Dragon Ball Daima Finale Opened Doors for the Sequel

As of now, there’s no official confirmation regarding upcoming projects related to the franchise. Dragon Ball Daima’s post-credit scene left room for the story to develop later on. Unexpectedly, the third eye, which granted immense power to the previous Demon Kings, wasn’t a unique item, as there are two more available at a mysterious store selling strange, status-altering consumables called medi-bugs, sky seeds, and so on. There was no explanation about where the eyes come from and why they grant someone that much power to those who consume them. The unanswered question confirms that much of the Demon Realm is still unexplored, and fans might never get the chance to know more about it.

However, that doesn’t change the fact that the ending was wholesome, and there’s no guarantee that there will be a sequel. The anime was released for a single season, and even if the animation studio decides to continue it, the story might fall short of expectations since it won’t be Toriyama’s original work. It might be best to bid farewell to this exceptional story since it already had the best possible ending for not only Goku and his friends, but even for some villains as well.

How did you feel about Akira Toriyama’s final project, and his legacy for the future of the Dragon Ball franchise? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: New Dragon Ball Super Remake Changes One of Vegeta’s Most Iconic Scenes
content:
Dragon Ball Super is now in the midst of a new remake anime airing new episodes this Fall , and the newest episode of Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has made a very noticeable change to one of Vegeta’s most iconic moments from the original. Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has been an intriguing remake to see play out as while it’s not deviating too far from the way the original TV anime series played out, there have been some noticeable differences that fans have been able to point out thus far.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has enhanced and retooled the original TV anime with new visual effects, new cuts of animation, new sound design and more. It’s led to some major moments getting a much needed upgrade like the first fight between Beerus and Goku , but changing Vegeta’s first confrontation with Beerus and his anger over Bulma might ultimately turn out to be a worse affair. Check out how it changed as spotted by @Z3RO_GRAVITY_ on X.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Just Made Vegeta’s “My Bulma!” Moment Worse

Though Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has thankfully gotten to this moment much faster than in the original Dragon Ball Super TV anime, it’s made what is a big characterization change to Beerus with it . In the classic version of the anime and Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods , Beerus slaps Bulma down to the ground after she had slapped him in the face. But in this newly retooled version of the scene, Bulma grabs onto Beerus and in the midst of shaking her off, Beerus elbows her in the face (accidentally) and she falls to the ground. But like both times, Vegeta explodes with rage.

Depending on which version or dub you watch in the moment, Vegeta cries out over his Bulma and fully goes into the fight against Beerus with Super Saiyan 2. This new version also changes a bit of how this actually looks in motion as Vegeta gets more of a purple aura for the occasion too. This is potentially a subtle tease of the path that Vegeta will go down later in future arcs with his own version of training with Hakai . If that’s indeed the case, it makes this moment all the better despite softening Beerus with his violence against Bulma.

What Does This Mean for Dragon Ball Super: Beerus ?

It’s a change that’s arguably better than the original because it does not depict as direct of violence against women, but in softening Beerus’ edge it also softens Vegeta’s own reaction to it. He’s angered, but the amount of rage he experiences in the first two depictions of the scene have become so memorable because of that initial moment with Bulma. By taking that away, it also takes away a moment where Vegeta decides to fully take on a god despite the consequences . It’s a point of no return in many ways.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus won’t be changing too much from the way the original TV played out, but it seems like there will be changes like this that fans will need to keep an eye out for either way. Because while it won’t be changes significant enough to greatly alter events as much as fans of the Dragon Ball Super manga had been hoping for , there will be shifts like this that make it all the more intriguing.

You can catch the newest episodes of Dragon Ball Super: Beerus streaming with Hulu and Crunchyroll, and a week later on Netflix. What do you think of this change to one of Vegeta’s most iconic scenes? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: 'Houseki no Kuni' Creator Launches New Manga
content:
The December 2026 issue of Monthly Afternoon magazine announced on Friday that manga creator Haruko Ichikawa will launch a new sci-fi manga, titled Cosmic Mimimi , in the magazine next issue, scheduled for a November 25 release.

Haruko is best known for Houseki no Kuni ( Land of the Lustrous ), which ran in Monthly Afternoon magazine from October 2012 to April 2024. The 13th and final volume went on sale on November 2024.

Kodansha USA licensed the manga in October 2016 and published the 13th volume on November 2025.

Produced by Orange , a 12-episode television anime adaptation aired in Fall 2017. Hidive streamed the anime with subtitles and dubs in multiple languages.

Haruko is best known for Houseki no Kuni ( Land of the Lustrous ), which ran in Monthly Afternoon magazine from October 2012 to April 2024. The 13th and final volume went on sale on November 2024.
Kodansha USA licensed the manga in October 2016 and published the 13th volume on November 2025.
Produced by Orange , a 12-episode television anime adaptation aired in Fall 2017. Hidive streamed the anime with subtitles and dubs in multiple languages.

title: Major Villainess Anime Teases 2027 Crunchyroll Return With New Trailer – Watch Now
content:
A major villainess anime is gearing up for its return to Crunchyroll with new episodes next year, and Though I Am an Inept Villainess is teasing some big events in the second half of its run with a new trailer. If you love anime like The Apothecary Diaries for how it explores an ancient Chinese inspired historical setting , then this one is right up your alley as it scratches that same itch as a villainess concubine uses magic to swap bodies with the most popular one in her ranks.

The anime adaptation for Satsuki Nakamura’s Though I am an Inept Villainess light novel series made its debut earlier this Summer and quickly got a lot of attention for fans. It’s coming back for its second half of episodes next year, and has revealed the first real trailer showing off what fans can expect to see in the coming season. You can check out the trailer for Though I am an Inept Villainess Part 2 in the video below.

When Does Though I am an Inept Villainess Part 2 Come Out?

Though I am an Inept Villainess Part 2 is currently scheduled to make its debut sometime in January as part of the Winter 2027 anime schedule . It has yet to confirm a concrete release date as of this time, but the new episodes will once again be streaming with Crunchyroll and Hulu alongside their debuts in Japan. That’s also where you can catch up with everything that’s happened in the anime thus far. It will also feature a returning production staff and voice cast as seen with the first half of the debut season.

Though I am an Inept Villainess Part 2 will be adapting “The Royal Outing Arc” when it returns for its episodes in January , and will be adding a few new members to the voice cast for the occasion. Yuichi Nakamura is joining the returning voice cast from the first half of the season as Rerien’s eldest brother Keikou, Shunichi Toki as her second-eldest brother Keishou, and Chiaki Kobayashi as Unran, the leader of a village in the south. But we’ll soon see how they all factor into what’s coming in this arc.

What to Know for Though I am an Inept Villainess

Part of what has made Though I am an Inept Villainess successful with fans this year is not only the fact that it feels reminiscent of The Apothecary Diaries in terms of its setting and political maneuvering, but also the studio behind it bringing it all to life. Mitsue Yamazaki has been directing Though I Am an Inept Villainess for Doga Kobo with Yoshihoko Nakamura overseeing the series composition, Ai Kukuchi designing the characters, and Yukari Hashimoto composing the music with Toho Animation overseeing it all .

With Though I am an Inept Villainess not returning for its episodes until next year, there’s plenty of time to catch up with everything that’s happened so far. There’s been a lot of fun developments for the characters as they bob and weave around one another, and the extra dose of magic on top of it all makes it that much more intriguing. Are you going to check out Though I am an Inept Villainess Part 2 when it hits? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Cool Fantasy Anime Confirms Season 3 Return Despite Season 2 Troubles (First Look Revealed)
content:
A cool fantasy anime series you can now find streaming with Crunchyroll has confirmed that it’s now in the works on a third season with a first look at what’s next. There are a number of interesting fantasy anime series that fans can check out now that don’t have an Isekai hook at the center, and that’s been especially true in the last few years with some titles that have gone on to find success of their own. But Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World has had some trouble finding its way.

The anime adaptation for Kei Sazane and Ao Nekonabe’s Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World made its initial debut with its first season in 2020, and returned a few years later for its second season. But it was hit by a huge delay in its production through the course of its episodes, and eventually finished out its second season a year later. But despite all of these issues, Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World has now confirmed Season 3 is in the works. Check out the first look below.

Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World Season 3 Announced

Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World Season 3 has been announced to be in the works, but there has yet to be any word on its potential release window, date or international release plans as of this time. The fantasy anime series returned for its second season in 2024, but then was put on a year long delay midseason before returning for its full slate of episodes last year ( but seemingly not leaving a mark as a notable fantasy series, unfortunately ). So it might be a while before this new wave of episodes actually hits.

It also makes it surprising to find out that Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World Season 3 is going to feature a returning production staff from the first two seasons. Yuki Inaba will once again be handling directing duties and providing the scripts for the collaboration between Studio Palette and Silver Link, and Kaori Yoshikawa will be providing the character designs. Fans had noticed how differently the designs seemed to be from the first season, however, and it seems like the pattern is continuing with this third season by the look of things so far.

What Is Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World ?

Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World takes place in a world separated by war. A young soldier is sent to assassinate the mysterious “Ice Calamity Witch,” but upon meeting the two figure out that they shared quite a lot in common. Deciding to work together (and subsequently becoming traitors to their respective sides), it sparks a romance between the two that’s still unfolding as of the end of the second season. And this third season seems to take things even further in that direction.

With this first look at Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World Season 3 teasing an important new addition to the anime (who has yet to be cast as of this time), it seems there will be even more romantic shenanigans to keep an eye out for. Are you excited for Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World Season 3? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Solo Leveling Studio’s Next Big Anime Confirms 2027 Crunchyroll Release – Watch Trailer
content:
The studio behind hits like Solo Leveling and Sword Art Online has a new anime coming to Crunchyroll at the start of the new year , and a trailer is helping to usher in its debut. A-1 Pictures has been at the center of some of the most notable anime releases thanks to the amount of time and effort that their teams put into each of their new releases. But while there are monster action hits like Solo Leveling , some of A-1 Pictures standouts are the furthest thing from it.

Yukino Sonoyama’s Bless is the next major manga to be picked up for an anime adaptation with a team at A-1 Pictures , and it’s set to make its debut in Japan this January. But a new update from Crunchyroll has now revealed that fans will be able to exclusively stream the new series with the platform outside of Japan when it hits next year. You can check out the new trailer for Bless to help celebrate its upcoming Crunchyroll premiere.

Bless Anime Confirms January 2027 Release With Crunchyroll

Bless is currently scheduled to make its debut in Japan sometime in January as part of the Winter 2027 anime schedule, and will be streaming with Crunchyroll in worldwide territories excluding Japan and China. No concrete release date has been announced for the anime as of this time, but it’s already looking like one of the more notable new releases kicking off the new year. Especially when looking at the production staff behind it all such as Shotaro Kitamura serving as director and Takayuki Kikuchi as assistant director for A-1 Pictures.

Fukurou Kamiza will be providing the scripts for the new Bless anime with Ryo Yoshimata composing the music, Honoko Yokoyama providing the character designs and serving as chief animation director alongside Tetsuya Kawakami and Reina Iwasaki. The voice cast for the series currently includes Tomohiro Ono as Aia Udagawa, Chiyuki Miura as Jun Sumisaki, Nobuhiko Okamoto as Ginga Yoyogi, Yoshino Aoyama as Oroka Sumeragi, Momoka Terasawa as Shitataka Sumeragi, Kentaro Kumagai as MM, Yoshiki Nakajima as Joe Osaki, Koki Uchiyama as Akiharu Nakano, and Tarusuke Shingaki as Hikaru Oya.

What Is Bless About Anyway?

It’s even more important to see a production team at A-1 Pictures taking the reins for this one as Bless is focused a lot on reflections of beauty and the uphill battle for the fashion industry. The series introduces two young students who have very different dreams. One has the looks to be a model, but wants to be a makeup artist instead. The other a shy girl who hides her face because of her freckles. But in working together, the two form a powerful team that rise through the fashion world bit by bit.

For a series about looking good and what that means to different people, it’s going to be very important for the anime to look just as good in its translation of it. If it’s going to be taken seriously with the way it breaks down the fashion industry’s standards of beauty, then the anime really needs to meet the task in all aspects too. But what are you hoping to see from Bless ‘ anime premiere? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Shonen Jump’s Best New Anime Confirms 2027 Return for Season 2 – Watch First Look Trailer
content:
One of the best new anime making the jump from Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine is coming back for Season 2 next year, and has now dropped the first real look at what to expect with a new trailer. It’s been a wild couple of years for Shonen Jump as not only have some of their longer running franchises have come to an end, but some of their strongest rookie hits have made their anime adaptation debuts. And the anime for Yuki Suenaga and Takamasa Moue’s Akane-banashi has been one of the strongest .

Akane-banashi made its debut earlier this year with a first season introducing even more fans to the successful franchise, and it’s setting up to return for its second season next January. While the initial confirmation of the new season didn’t come with much information about what we’re going to see in the new season, Akane-banashi Season 2 has now dropped a new trailer and poster revealing a fuller look at new characters and more. You can check it out below.

Akane-banashi Season 2 Confirms January 2027 Release With New Trailer

Akane-banashi Season 2 will be making its debut sometime in January as part of the Winter 2027 anime schedule , but a concrete release date or international platforms have yet to be confirmed for the new episodes as of this time. The new additions to the voice cast revealed in this trailer include Taku Yashiro as Asagao Konjakutei and Yoji Ueda as Hassho Tsubakiya, but their roles in the coming arc will be revealed in due time. As for that arc itself, Akane is going to take on her next level of training following the events of the first season.

With Akane officially becoming a Zenza as of the end of the first season , the coming arc will see her learning more about the art of Rakugo as she further figures out how to carve out her place in the art form. There she will meet even more rivals and potential teachers, but it’s going to all be building on everything fans had gotten to see in the first season. If we’re lucky, it’s also going to have the same team behind it all as the full production staff has yet to be confirmed for the episodes as of this time.

What to Know for Akane-banashi

If you missed out on Akane-banashi’ s debut season following its premiere earlier this Spring, it’s actually one of the easiest anime to catch up with. Not only is it streaming with platforms like Netflix (complete with an English dub) , but it’s also available completely for free with its global streaming YouTube channel. This made it a little bit of an underdog when stacked up against some of the other huge releases through the year, but also makes it one of the more easily accessible anime for curious fans.

Akane-banashi has one of the more notable Shonen Jump heroes that fans have gotten to see in recent memory. It’s not an action-focused series by any means, but seeing Akane chase after her dreams in the very same way that the other Shonen fighters do makes her even more compelling than the others. But are you going to jump into Akane-banashi heading into Season 2? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: After 22 Years, Bleach Reveals First Look & Synopsis for Anime Finale Timeskip
content:
Bleach is officially set to end after 22 long years of the anime, and has revealed the first look and story details for the final episode of the anime ever. Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity went on hiatus for a month to better prepare for the final two episodes of the series , and the first of these episodes had brought the long fight against Yhwach to its ultimate end. But with the final fight over, it’s left the anime to say goodbye with one final episode coming next.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity is only a day away from the premiere of the anime’s final episode ever, and to celebrate has revealed the first look at what’s coming in the finale. Set ten years after the fight against Yhwach came to an end ( which fans saw in the anime’s penultimate episode ), the final episode of the anime reveals the future lives of all three worlds as the long running story prepares to end. Check out the first look images for Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Episode 50 below.

When Does Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Episode 50 Come Out?

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Episode 50 will be making its debut with Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ in the United States on Monday, October 26th at 11:30PM E T. Titled “Death & Strawberry,” the synopsis for the episode teases a full adaptation of the original epilogue seen in Tite Kubo’s Bleach manga finale with a ten year jump into the future, “Ten years have passed since the battle known as the Great War to Protect the Soul King. The Seireitei, reduced to ashes in the fierce battle against Yhwach, had gradually recovered and regained peace as reconstruction progressed.”

But as the synopsis continues, it seems like there’s another issue popping up for one final confrontation, “On the day that construction on the final reconstruction area was completed, new captains were about to be appointed to the Thirteen Court Guard Squads. On this auspicious day with a clear blue sky, the Research and Development Bureau sensed an ominous spiritual pressure at the same time as the inauguration ceremony…” But as fans of Bleach’ s original manga know by now , it’s either a true end or a new beginning.

What’s Next for Bleach After the Anime Ends?

With Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War coming to an end with Episode 50, this is also the end of the original Bleach TV anime series that began 22 years ago. It had been canceled before it got to adapt the final arc of Kubo’s manga, and that meant that fans had waited over a decade to see it all come to fruition. There’s a lot riding on this grand finale as fans are eager to see what’s next , and there could actually end up being much more in the future if we’re lucky enough to see it all continue.

Bleach creator Tite Kubo actually released a special one-shot story after the finale a few years ago, and with it actually sparked an entire new arc teasing returning villains, a whole new realm and more . It’s yet to be revealed if the anime franchise will ever touch these materials in the future, but for now this is likely the end. What are you hoping to see in Bleach’ s final episode? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!
